note: Publication status describes the recorded source of each contribution: unpublished means no paper is recorded for that work. Participant credit is separate from verification, and does not by itself establish global priority. Reproductions are credited as computations of published results. Participant work is credited to the vxvware organisation.

contributions.title: G-matrices at n=49, contradicting a published nonexistence statement
contributions.summary: [@djokovic2018goethals] report a complete classification of cyclic families with symmetric or skew blocks for odd v < 50 and find none of type (kkss) at v=49, where the only parameter set of that type is (49; 24,24,22,18; 39). The vxvware census finds eight quadruples with exactly that parameter set, one equiv-v1 class, and the rows verify exactly on this board. The same program reproduces the published counts at v=33, 37, 41, 43, and 45.

contributions.title: G-matrix censuses at n=51, 55, 57, and 59
contributions.summary: Complete vxvware censuses past the range classified by Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals]: four classes at n=51, three at n=55, none at n=57, and eight quadruples at n=59 that the source counts as two classes and equiv-v1 as one. Existence at 51 and 55 was already known from Spence's infinite family [@spence1977skew] (q = 101 and 109); the class counts at 51 and 55, the nonexistence at 57, and the existence and count at 59 are new. Replays with pinned engines between 2026-11-14 and 2026-11-15 returned the same classes at each order, so the four counts are exact. The empty cell at 53 is not a search result: a (kkss) parameter set exists only when 2v - 1 is a sum of two squares, by the parameter-set condition of [@djokovic2018goethals], and 105 is not.

contributions.title: G-matrices at n=61, first existence and two classes
contributions.summary: The exhaustive vxvware gmat_c census at n=61, the first open G-matrix order, found a (kkss) quadruple with row sums (1, 1, -11, -11) in its ninth piece on 2026-10-18 and finished all 32 pieces on 2026-10-22 after 811 cpu-hours: twelve quadruples, two equiv-v1 classes (three under the source's own convention, which does not transpose blocks). Spence's family [@spence1977skew] does not reach 61, Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals] classify through 49, and the 2009 table of cyclic families in [@djokovic2009supplementary] leaves type (kkss) unresolved at (61; 30, 30, 25, 25; 49), the only parameter set of that type at 61. The rows verify exactly; the count of two became exact on 2026-11-15, when a replay with the pinned kkss-census-c-v3 engine returned the same classes. The first quadruple keeps its hand-entered id and the census maps its class onto it.

contributions.title: Good matrices at n=53, 55, and 61
contributions.summary: The vxvware census found good matrices at three orders no published search covers: 104 rows at n=53, 40 at n=55, and 120 at n=61, each yielding one equiv-v1 class. The rows verify exactly; replays with the pinned good-census-c-v1 engine on 2026-11-14 to 2026-11-16 returned the same classes, so the three counts are exact. At 55 a repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes] reports an independent exhaustive classification with exactly one class; it cites this board for existence.

contributions.title: Good-matrix census at n=59, empty
contributions.summary: Two independent complete runs of the vxvware census report no good matrices at n=59. The board records the attributed claim without a verification tier because the search has not been replayed here.

contributions.title: Orbit-restricted G-matrix search at n=63
contributions.summary: A search with the two skew rows constant on the orbits of the subgroup generated by 4 reproduces the known Spence example [@spence1977skew] at parameters (63; 31,31,27,25; 51). It is not a census and establishes no count.

contributions.title: Independent G-matrix censuses through n=45
contributions.summary: The vxvware census recomputes type kkss at every admissible odd order through 45 and agrees with the class counts published by Đoković and Kotsireas [@djokovic2018goethals] at 33, 37, 41, 43, and 45. The imported rows fill the published-not-imported cells with exactly verified representatives.

contributions.title: Best-matrix nonexistence campaign at n=73
contributions.summary: The vxvware campaign reports no best matrices at n=73. This is participant work beyond the published baseline, retained as an archived nonexistence claim; the 104,500-class legacy identity gap still prevents a stronger verification tier.

contributions.title: Skew families at n=73
contributions.summary: The vxvware sweep generated 15,360 quadruples, yielding eight verified equiv-v1 classes. Published skew-Hadamard existence at order 292, by a construction of Đoković recorded by Cati and Pasechnik [@cati2024database], is credited separately; these are participant-generated families, without a claim of first existence at this order.

contributions.title: Good-matrix nonexistence campaign at n=65
contributions.summary: The campaign reports nonexistence. A missing early receipt chain leaves this an archived claim, with participant credit retained. A repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes] reports an independent exhaustive search of 67,437 compressed instances that found no good matrices of order 65; it describes this board's claim as unverified.

contributions.title: Good-matrix partial search at n=67
contributions.summary: Participant search with partial coverage from the withdrawn first run; it does not establish nonexistence. The complete census that does is recorded separately as good-67-empty.

contributions.title: Row-sum obstruction for one restricted family at n=89 (order-11 coset unions)
contributions.summary: No quadruple at n=89 has one skew block and all four blocks unions of cosets of the order-11 subgroup of the multiplier group of Z_89, each with or without 0. A skew block has row sum 1, so the squared row sums of the other three blocks must add to 4n - 1 = 355, and no three row sums of such coset unions do. This excludes only that family and says nothing about other quadruples at n=89: the verified quadruples in the cell each have a skew block of this kind and three blocks outside the family.

contributions.title: Independent good-matrix computation at n=41
contributions.summary: An independent campaign for the nonexistence result of Bright, Đoković, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2019good]. The archived coverage is receipt-backed; the board has not replayed the GPU search.

contributions.title: Independent best-matrix censuses through n=43
contributions.summary: The vxvware exact census implementation independently enumerates the small orders classified by Bright, Đoković, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2019best]. The board reports exact counts only when its full replay succeeds.

contributions.title: Skew quadruple at n=119
contributions.summary: A cyclic skew quadruple of order 119, giving a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 476, posted on 2026-10-23 in the repository github.com/vatskishan03/Hadamard with no accompanying paper. Imported from its certificate; the discovery is the repository author’s.

contributions.title: Published constructions and catalogue imports
contributions.summary: Imported reference constructions retain the original source attribution. Inclusion in the challenge catalogue does not make the importer their discoverer. The Williamson entries include every class of Holzmann, Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie [@holzmann2008williamson] through order 59, and both classes at 63 and the Turyn class [@turyn1972infinite] at 69 from the MathCheck enumeration of Bright, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2018enumeration] [@bright2020williamson].

contributions.title: Good-matrix census at n=67, empty
contributions.summary: The re-run of the vxvware census with the corrected wide-word engine, validated against the stored n=37 census before every shard and run as sixteen resumable shards on two hosts from 2026-10-27 to 2026-11-10, reports no good matrices at n=67 after 11.76e12 triples. The board records the attributed claim without a verification tier because the search has not been replayed here.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=65, 67, 69 and 71 by pool join
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=65, 67, 69 and 71, found on 2026-11-19 by the sampling search in research/starter/skew: the skew block is fixed in advance, invariant under a multiplier subgroup of odd order, and the other three blocks are sampled inside per-lag autocorrelation windows and joined exactly. The skew-Hadamard orders 260, 268, 276 and 284 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all four orders: constructions of 1992 at 65 and 67 are recounted in [@djokovic1994five], 69 is in [@djokovic2023skew], and 71 belongs to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 283). The search is not a census and says nothing about how many classes exist.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=93, 95, 97 and 113 by orbit search
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=93, 95, 97 and 113, found on 2026-11-20 by the orbit-restricted searches in research/starter/skew: all four blocks are constant on the orbits of a multiplier subgroup of odd order (5, 9, 3 and 7). The quadruples at 93, 95 and 113 come from the exhaustive search of that orbit space (complete at 95 and 113, stopped at the tenth solution at 93), the one at 97 from the pool join restricted to it. The skew-Hadamard orders 372, 380, 388 and 452 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all four orders: constructions of 1992 at 93 and 113 are recounted in [@djokovic1994five], 95 belongs to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 379), and 97 is in [@djokovic2008skew]. The searches cover one orbit space each and are not a census of the cells.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=77, 103, 105, 109, 111, 117, 121 and 123 by orbit-restricted pool join
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=77, 103, 105, 109, 111, 117, 121 and 123, found on 2026-11-20 by the pool join of research/starter/skew restricted to quadruples in which all four blocks are constant on the orbits of a multiplier subgroup: order 3 at 77, 103, 105, 109, 111 and 117, order 5 at 121 and 123. The skew block and the row sums are fixed by the plan; the runs at 77 and 109 found one solution each, the run at 105 two, the others between 7 and 86. The skew-Hadamard orders 308, 412, 420, 436, 444, 468, 484 and 492 are not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json; these are the board's first quadruples with a skew block at those n, without a claim of first existence. Quadruples with a skew block over the cyclic group were already published at all eight orders: 77, 105, 111, 117 and 123 belong to the family of [@xia2005infinite] for prime powers q = 4n - 1 (q = 307, 419, 443, 467 and 491), 103 is in [@djokovic1994five], which also recounts a construction of 1992 at 121, and 109 is in [@djokovic2008orders]. The searches are samples of one orbit space each and are not a census of the cells.

contributions.title: Skew quadruples at n=83 and 125 from the Paley matrices
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at each of n=83 and 125, in the form A skew, B symmetric, C = D that [@xia2005infinite] proves to exist for every prime power q = 4n - 1 (q = 331 and 499). The rows were generated on 2026-11-21 from the Paley matrices [@paley1933orthogonal] of orders 332 and 500 by the script recorded in evidence/literature/paley-four-circulant.txt; they were not transcribed from the source. These are literature constructions, not new results and not search results, and the credit is the source's. The board had no quadruple with a skew block at those n before.

contributions.title: Skew quadruple at n=81 over the cyclic group by compression search
contributions.summary: One quadruple with a skew block at n=81 over the cyclic group Z_81, found on 2026-11-21 by a search that fixes the skew block and the 3-compressions of the other three blocks, enumerates every lift of each compressed block, keeps the lifts whose periodic autocorrelations lie in five-value windows, and joins the three pools exactly. The search code is not in the repository; the run record is evidence/participants/compression/skew-81.txt. A skew-Hadamard matrix of order 324 has been known since 1994, from supplementary difference sets in the elementary abelian group of order 81 [@djokovic1994five]; the order is not new and is not among the open orders of baselines/skew-gaps.json. The board's entry is over the cyclic group. A search of current sources on 2026-11-21 found no earlier quadruple with a skew block over Z_81; that is a report of the search, not a proof of priority, and no first existence is claimed. This is the board's first quadruple with a skew block at n=81. The join stopped at its first solution, so the search is a sample and not a census.

contributions.title: Williamson census at n=65, empty, confirming earlier public records
contributions.summary: The board's compression census at n=65 lifted all 72,478 of its compressed instances and found no Williamson matrices; the census entry is dated 2026-11-14. Two public records are earlier and report the same result: a Zenodo preprint whose version 1 is dated 2026-10-22 [@graham2026williamson65], and a repository note in a commit dated 2026-10-25 [@kishan2026notes]. Neither is peer reviewed. The board's run is an independent confirmation, not a first result. Each of the earlier records counts 70,699 compressed instances against the board's 72,478; the difference has not been reconciled.

contributions.title: Williamson census at n=61, one class, reproducing a published classification
contributions.summary: Lang and Schneider [@lang2012turyn] report in their introduction that they implemented the exhaustive algorithm of Holzmann, Kharaghani and Tayfeh-Rezaie [@holzmann2008williamson], extended its results from order 59 to order 61, and found exactly one equivalence class of Williamson matrices of order 61, which is of Turyn type; Bright, Kotsireas and Ganesh [@bright2020williamson] cite the enumeration at 61 to that paper. Only the first two pages of [@lang2012turyn] were read for this record. The board's own census is a full run of the pinned engine williamson-hkt-v2 on 2026-11-14 (17,359 s on 8 threads), registered as a replay: it returned one class, the Turyn-type quadruple already on the board, so the board's count agrees with the published one. The run is an independent reproduction of a published classification, not a first result.

contributions.title: Two skew quadruples at n=89: a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356
contributions.summary: Two quadruples with a skew block at n=89 over the cyclic group Z_89, found on 2026-11-22 by two slices of one run. The Goethals–Seidel matrix of each is a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356. The search fixes a skew first block invariant under the multiplier group of order 11, collects rows of the other three blocks whose periodic autocorrelations lie in fixed windows into three pools, and joins the pools exactly. The two quadruples share the skew block and differ in the other three blocks, which have no symmetry. It is a sampling search: these are two solutions, not a census. The search code is not in the repository; the run record is evidence/participants/pool-join/skew-89.txt, written before the second quadruple was reported. Order 356 is the smallest order for which the existence of a skew-Hadamard matrix is stated to be undecided in [@djokovic2023skew]; it is given as the smallest unknown order in [@araya2024classification] and as the smallest open order in the survey [@egan2026recent]; the database of [@cati2024database] has no construction for it; and it is the smallest open order of baselines/skew-gaps.json. A search of the literature and public repositories on 2026-11-22 found no earlier skew-Hadamard matrix of order 356; that is a report of the search, not a proof of priority, and the result has not been reviewed.
